newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Telekom H1 net profit drops sharply.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Telekom H1 net profit drops sharply.

text.p: German telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom AG said on Tuesday its group net profit in the half to June 30 fell to 130 million marks ($86 million) from 700 million in the year-earlier half.
Group income from ordinary activities rose to 2.7 billion marks from 2.2 billion as sales grew to 29.7 billion from 29.3 billion.
Telekom said it would pay out 1.5 billion marks in dividends to shareholders in 1996, the year of its landmark initial public offerering.

In an unusual move to attract new shareholders for its November share launch, chief finance officer Joachim Kroeske said the company would announce in its investor prospectus the dividend new shareholders would receive in 1997 as well.
"In the first year after our listing, we will be able to pay a dividend that will rank among the highest in Germany," Kroske told journalists, commenting on the 1997 payout.
The company expects profit to continue increasing from 1997 onwards. "The improvement in the results will accelerate beginning in 1997," Kroske said.

Telekom said it expected full-year 1996 group turnover of about 62 billion marks, down from 66.1 billion marks, and profit from ordinary activities of about eight billion marks, up from 3.8 billion in 1995. Two billion marks of sales are attributable to the consolidation of Hungarian telephone company Matav.

Kroeske attributed an 11.8 percent fall in telephone services revenue in the first half to uncertainty among customers after rate changes that took effect on January 1, a software glitch that overcharged customers on January 1, and the shutting down of certain services.
